{"markdown":"# Issues Memo — IBM e-business Hosting Agreement (Base Terms)

**To:** Deal team | **From:** In-house counsel | **Re:** Playbook review findings (document reference: § 3.1 Term)

## Executive summary

We have completed the playbook review. Six rules are satisfied and require no redline: the vendor infringement indemnity in § 8.1 (which sits at, and on the super-cap element above, the fallback because indemnification payments are carved out of the damages cap by § 9.1(a)), and the absence of any exclusivity, non-compete, MFN, minimum-commitment or non-solicitation burden on us, aided by the Freedom of Action clause at § 14.16.

Eight rules deviate. The most significant are commercial-control items: the **licence grant in § 12.1 is expressly "revocable" and runs to Bluefly, Inc. only**, with no coverage for Affiliates or contractors; **assignment in § 14.10 binds only us**, leaving IBM free to assign without consent and without a competitor bar; **deliverables default to Type II**, giving us an enterprise-use-only licence with no perpetual term, modification or sublicensing right, while § 14.18 lets IBM exploit our contact data for marketing; and **IBM's investigation right in § 11.3 is unlimited as to frequency, notice and cost**. IBM's only performance warranty (§ 5.1(a)) is a care-and-skill standard with no conformance warranty, duration or remedy, and § 5.2/§ 5.4 make that set exclusive. Section 9 caps are mutual at twelve months of charges but contain **no carve-out for confidentiality breach, gross negligence or wilful misconduct**, and § 6 expressly subordinates confidentiality to §§ 5, 9 and 10.

Two rules are **missing** entirely: post-termination transition assistance, Content return and deletion (§ 3.5 addresses only accrued payment obligations), and any vendor insurance covenant — both material given that IBM hosts the environment and processes personal information on our behalf under § 14.18.

Two findings (**RENEWAL** and **T4C**) are marked *needs review* and did not pass verification; they should not be relied on or sent to IBM until re-verified against the executed text.

## Findings

| Severity | Rule | Status | Section |
|---|---|---|---|
| Critical | INDEMN — Indemnification by Vendor | Compliant (at fallback) | § 8.1 Indemnification by IBM |
| High | ASSIGN — Assignment and change of control | Deviation | § 14.10 Assignment |
| High | EXCLUSIVITY — Exclusivity binding Customer | Compliant | § 14.16 Freedom of Action |
| High | IP — Ownership of deliverables and Customer Data | Deviation | § 5.4 Other Disclaimers (with §§ 7.0, 14.17, 14.18) |
| High | LICENSE — Licence grant scope | Deviation | § 12.1 License |
| High | NONCOMPETE — Non-compete on Customer | Compliant | § 14.16 Freedom of Action |
| Medium | AUDIT — Audit rights against Customer | Deviation | § 11.3 Suspected Violations |
| Medium | GOVLAW — Governing law and venue | Deviation | § 14.3 Choice of Law |
| Medium | LD — Liquidated damages payable by Customer | Deviation | § 3.4 Termination for Convenience |
| Medium | MFN — Most-favoured-nation obligations | Compliant | § 14.16 Freedom of Action |
| Medium | MINCOMMIT — Minimum purchase commitments | Compliant | § 4.1 Charges |
| Medium | NOSOLICIT — Non-solicitation binding Customer | Compliant | § 14.8 Personnel |
| Medium | RENEWAL — Auto-renewal and notice window | Needs review (verification failed) | § 3.2 Renewal |
| Medium | T4C — Termination for convenience | Needs review (verification failed) | § 3.4 Termination for Convenience |
| Medium | TRANSITION — Transition assistance and data return | Missing | § 3.5 Effect of Termination |
| Medium | WARRANTY — Performance warranty and duration | Deviation | § 5.1 IBM Representations and Warranties |
| Low | INSURANCE — Vendor insurance | Missing | § 14.12 Risk of Loss |
| Low | LOL-CAP — Liability cap, mutuality and carve-outs | Deviation | § 9.1 IBM's Limitation of Liability |

## Walk-away items

The following findings sit in, or approach, walk-away territory under our playbook and should be treated as conditions of signature rather than negotiating preferences:

1. **§ 12.1 — revocable licence excluding Affiliates and contractors (LICENSE, high).** A licence revocable at IBM's discretion, granted to Bluefly, Inc. alone and confirmed by § 14.17 as granting no other rights, is walk-away. We require deletion of at-will revocability, extension to Affiliates and contractors acting on our behalf, termination only for uncured material breach, and confirmation that the § 7.0(c) paid-up Type II licence is perpetual.
2. **§ 11.3 — unlimited, unannounced investigation right (AUDIT, medium).** No frequency cap, no advance notice of the investigation itself, no cost allocation, coupled with an obligation to hand over all relevant information on request. We require the three fallback limits (frequency, notice, cost).
3. **No vendor insurance (INSURANCE, low severity but structurally material).** IBM hosts the environment and processes personal information under § 14.18; a data-processing vendor carrying no insurance is walk-away. We require the preferred covenant as a new § 14.21, with the E&O USD 1M / cyber USD 2M fallback available.
4. **§ 5.1/§ 5.2/§ 5.4 — care-and-skill warranty only (WARRANTY, medium).** The bargain fails every fallback element and approaches walk-away; we require the inserted 90-day software / 30-day Services conformance warranty with repair, replacement and refund remedies, drafted inside § 5.1 so § 5.2's exclusivity preserves rather than swallows it.

## Next steps

1. **Re-verify RENEWAL (§ 3.2) and T4C (§ 3.4) before circulating.** Both failed verification. Once confirmed, our positions are a sixty (60) day non-renewal window with renewal charges capped at 105% of the prior term, and a convenience right exercisable at any time on thirty (30) days' notice with pro-rata refund of prepaid charges (fallback: an express three-month cap in § 3.4(b)).
2. **Issue the redline** on the eight deviations and two missing clauses, in the order of the walk-away list above, with the drafted inserts for § 3.5 (transition assistance, Content return within 30 days in a standard machine-readable format, certified deletion) and new § 14.21 (insurance).
3. **Add the mutual carve-out as new § 9.3** for breach of confidentiality obligations, gross negligence and wilful misconduct. If accepted, we then pursue the preferred-level points noted under LOL-CAP (USD 1,000,000 cap floor, fraud and IP carve-outs, exclusion of our payment obligations, and § 9.1(c)(2)'s disclaimer of liability for loss of or damage to our records or data).
4. **Fix venue.** § 14.3 already selects New York law (our preference) but the Agreement has no forum or dispute-resolution clause; add exclusive jurisdiction in the state and federal courts in New York County with a carve-out for temporary injunctive relief.
5. **Cap the exit charge.** Adopt the fallback in § 3.4(b) — three months' charges for the terminated Services as the sole liquidated amount payable by us — rather than deleting the charge, to avoid a dangling cross-reference in § 3.3. Confirm whether an Attachment A charge schedule exists; none appears in the document reviewed.
6. **Escalation triggers.** If IBM refuses the § 12.1, § 11.3, insurance or warranty positions, escalate before further concessions. Separately, if any Order Form term exceeds twelve months, escalate to fix renewal terms at twelve months. If the deal permits a further ask on indemnity (currently compliant), we would add IBM cover for breach of applicable law, vendor-caused data breach and gross negligence/wilful misconduct, and trim § 8.2(a)(3)."}
